How does Python manage memory and garbage collection?

Supplied answer
Python keeps objects in a private heap and manages it automatically. Each object has a reference count;
when the count drops to zero the memory is released. A cyclic garbage collector (the gc module)
additionally cleans up objects that reference each other. Small integers and short strings are cached and
reused, which is why 'is' can behave surprisingly with small numbers.
